people._note: who runs this workspace (asked at first-run setup)

identity._note: paths to the brand's own identity files, absolute or relative to this copy

colors._note: theme = the kit theme picked at setup (studio, harbor, ochre or ink). Each reel's reel.json uses {"theme": {"preset": <theme>, "accent": <accent>}}; background and ink only if the brand has its own.

loop._note: The reel loop (/reel-loop). All optional. viral_views_multiple: how many times the median views counts as a breakout (default 5); viral_min_views: and at least this many (default 5000); min_hours: hours a reel is out before it is judged (default 72); min_views_to_judge: views before its skip rate means anything (default 500); stall_after: judged reels in a row with no better skip rate before it says stalled (default 6).

reels._note: Where reel folders sit under reels/. "flat" (default) = reels/<slug>. "dated" = reels/2026/11 November/November 12/<slug>, by the day the reel is planned to post. Every script finds a reel in either place. New reels follow this setting; move the ones you have with `kit organize --layout dated` (it shows the moves first, --apply does them) and back with --layout flat.

posting._note: How this brand's reels get posted: "by hand" (default), "instagram-scheduler", "tool: <name>" or "own publisher". Set with /reel-posting. Timezone for scheduling, e.g. America/Toronto. days and times: the brand's posting days (e.g. ["tue", "thu"]) and times on each of them, any number a day (one: ["18:00"]; several: ["09:00", "13:00", "19:00"]), set with /content-calendar days; every time on a posting day is one slot, and the calendar marks empty ones as open. time is the older single time, still read when times is empty. platforms = where every reel goes with the kit's publisher, e.g. ["instagram", "facebook", "threads"]; empty = Instagram only; schedule.mjs uses it when --platforms is not given, and /reel-posting asks about it once, not per reel. A reel's time comes from its row in brand/plan.md (schedule.mjs --from-plan).

dashboard._note: The content dashboard (/content-calendar, docs/dashboard.md). OFF until the brand owner turns each part on: instagram, facebook, threads = read this brand's own numbers on each through Meta's APIs (docs/connect.md); telegram = send the summary to the owner's phone; refresh = off, daily or weekly, set by /content-calendar auto (time on this computer's clock). host = where the page is viewed: local (default), wifi, netlify (suggested), cloudflare or folder (any other host), set by /content-calendar host; site = the Netlify site id or Cloudflare Pages project; url = its address, for the Telegram link. publish_every = with a host set, the online copy follows your changes at most every this many minutes (0 = only on the scheduled refresh). Tokens live in ~/.config/bagelunit-reels/, written by the owner.

batch._note: The most reels Claude plans in one sitting for this brand (a week's worth: for several posts a day, the number a day times the posting days). Each reel is still approved on its own. Goals may repeat; angles may not in a batch of up to five, and in a bigger one no two reels next to each other share one.

autopilot._note: OFF by default. The brand owner turns a permission on, see template CLAUDE.md section 3b. retime = the daily refresh may move posting.times, and the plan rows not yet scheduled, to the hours the brand's own numbers favour (best-times.mjs; at most once a week, never a reel that is already scheduled).

updates._note: ON by default. true = at the start of a session, Claude checks once whether a newer kit version is out and tells you. It reads one public file from GitHub and never updates anything by itself.
